candidates.author: tanishqbaweja
candidates.title: fix(subtitle): split Thai and Lao scripts at the spaces between sentences
candidates.snippet: Thai and Lao text separates sentences with a space instead of a full stop. `split_string_by_punctuations()` ends a script line only at `PUNCTUATIONS` and at line breaks, so a Thai or Lao paragraph is one script line. With an Edge TTS voice and the default `subtitle_provider = "edge"`, the video then shows the whole narration as one subtitle: a 6-sentence script stands on screen as a 6-line block for all of its 16 seconds, and a longer one runs off the top of the frame. Thai is one of the 14 script languages in the WebUI (`th-TH` in `support_locales`), the voice list has `th-TH-PremwadeeNeural`
candidates.problem: Thai and Lao subtitles are not split into separate lines because the language uses spaces instead of full stops, causing the TTS subtitle generator to display an entire paragraph as a single long subtitle block.
candidates.selfBuiltSolution: Modified the split_string_by_punctuations function to also split Thai and Lao scripts at spaces between sentences, ensuring proper subtitle line breaks for Edge TTS output.
candidates.reasoning: The author identifies a niche localization issue with AI TTS subtitles and implements a concrete code change to solve it, indicating a genuine lead‑user signal.

candidates.snippet: WhisperWriter is a small dictation app that uses OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model to auto-transcribe recordings from a user's microphone. I built it with the help of ChatGPT (with GPT-4) and GitHub Copilot, with almost every line of code in the repository written by AI. Running the app: Everything you need to know to set WhisperWriter up is in the linked GitHub repo's README file. The app can be run locally using the open-source Whisper release or online through the OpenAI API. I personally use the latter because my computer is not very powerful, but the former is free
